### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **2** package(s): `@objectstack/core`, `@objectstack/metadata-protocol`, touching **2** documentable anchor(s). ⚠️ **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json`), so the pages documenting them are **NOT COVERED by this run** — this is not a clean bill of health for those files.

**1** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_

⛔ **3** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v16.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-0.mdx`  _(via ObjectStackProtocolImplementation (symbol, a top-level class))_
- `content/docs/releases/v17/17-1.mdx`  _(via searchAll (symbol, a method of class ObjectStackProtocolImplementation))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **1** changed file(s) yielded no anchor (`packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json`) — pages documenting those are invisible to this run
- the SDK route bridge reached **54** of **206** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **152** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **152**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **97** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **33** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8830c28056b9f466adfe9d59cd179b1d0fa6784` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `535aaacf1ae504571cc9dc7c4b5652febb1f17b5` — the merge of head `7e7d0eefe21459c34ed5a79f239146b42d832e04` into base `d8830c28056b9f466adfe9d59cd179b1d0fa6784`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin 535aaacf1ae504571cc9dc7c4b5652febb1f17b5 && git checkout 535aaacf1ae504571cc9dc7c4b5652febb1f17b5
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin d8830c28056b9f466adfe9d59cd179b1d0fa6784 7e7d0eefe21459c34ed5a79f239146b42d832e04 && git checkout -B drift-repro d8830c28056b9f466adfe9d59cd179b1d0fa6784 && git merge --no-ff 7e7d0eefe21459c34ed5a79f239146b42d832e04

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json d8830c28056b9f466adfe9d59cd179b1d0fa6784
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs d8830c28056b9f466adfe9d59cd179b1d0fa6784` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER`
Head-sha: `7e7d0eefe21459c34ed5a79f239146b42d832e04`
Local-runs: none

Inputs read: card #22640 (body, triage 6095397504, claim 6099181509, os-dev-report 6100391897), PR #22704 (body, 6-file list, net diff against main at merge base d8830c28, which is origin/main at read time), the head's check-runs (two reads, the second right before this post). Source context for judging the diff was read with git show against origin/main and the head only: api-derivation.ts, the surrounding searchAll loop, the canReadObject caller census, the analytics decision site, core's cross-package declaration and vitest repo project. Nothing was built, run or re-run.

**Check-runs on this head at the last read:** 31 total, 18 success, 3 skipped (Build Docs, Console Pin Gate, Packed-tarball smoke — not applicable to this diff), **10 still in progress**: Test Core 1/6–6/6, Lint & Repo Gates, Temporal Conformance (live PG + MySQL), Dogfood Regression Gate 3/3, Type Check · workspace. Concluded and green: Check Changeset (its ADR-0087 disposition step and launch-window major guard both success at step level), Governed Surface Queue Guard, Type Check · source gates / consumer gates / debt ledger, Build Core, Dogfood Verify CLI, Dogfood Regression Gate 1/3 and 2/3, the five PR-protocol checks, Check PR Size, docs link and docs-affected checks. This record judges the contract on what has concluded; the queue's "every check green" condition is the owning seat's to re-read at queue time, and it is not met yet.

### ① Derived judgments

Accept-set changes the diff implies, each judged:

1. **The served set of the cross-object search (`GET /search`, `searchAll`) narrows.** An object whose `enable.apiMethods` resolves to restricted-without-`list` (for example `['get']`), to deny-all (`[]`, or a non-array value, which `resolveEffectiveApiMethods` fails closed), or whose whitelist grants `list` beside `searchable: false`, is now skipped before it is queried, named or counted. **Right.** This is exactly what `apiExposureDenialReason(enable, 'search')` answers on main: `api-disabled` first, then `method-not-allowed` from the derivation row `search: { all: ['list'], flag: searchable !== false }`. The REST data routes, the dispatcher, MCP and the analytics door (`api-exposure-door.ts` lines 275 and 308) already turn that same answer into refusals, so the sweep now agrees with every other door. No second rule was written.
2. **Every previously skipped object stays skipped.** `apiEnabled: false` is the decision's first branch; `searchable: false` keeps an explicit skip. **Right**, and the explicit `searchable` line is necessary, not redundant: for an object with no whitelist the decision returns `null` at the `unrestricted` branch before any flag is read, so dropping that line would have WIDENED the sweep onto `{ searchable: false }` objects. The PR's table of seven `enable` shapes matches the source. The card allowed the flag to keep its meaning beside the decision "if the decision does not already cover it"; it does not cover it everywhere, so the line stays. The served set after this diff is a strict subset of the one before: **no widening anywhere in the diff.**
3. **The decision takes no caller.** Platform admins and context-less in-process calls skip the same objects. **Right** — this is the data routes' behaviour already; the sweep must not be the one door that serves an administrator rows the whitelist withholds.
4. **An explicit `objects=` naming a refused object answers like one naming no object** (silent skip, no 405). **Right for this door.** The sweep already answered a named `apiEnabled: false` object that way on main; the per-object 405 belongs to the data routes, which judge one object per request. A refused object leaves no trace in hits, pages, totals or object names, which the pin checks by `JSON.stringify`.
5. **Position in the loop.** The decision runs after the `objectsFilter` membership test and before the name-prefix skips and `canReadObject`. The PR body's "runs first in the loop" is loose prose (the filter is first), but the property it stands for holds: a refused object is never queried, never named, never counted, and the read admission is never asked about it (pinned by the `canReadObject.mock.calls` assertion). Not a defect.
6. **Public surface: unchanged.** No export of `@objectstack/metadata-protocol` is added, removed or re-typed; `packages/spec` is untouched (`canServeApiOperation` was already exported through `data/index.ts` and the file already imported from `@objectstack/spec/data`); the wire shape of `GET /search` is unchanged. The change is runtime behaviour of a published package, correctly classed as an accept-set narrowing and not a surface change.
7. **Triage's enumeration pin** (`packages/core/src/security/row-serving-door-exposure.pin.test.ts`). The discriminator (every non-test `.ts` under `packages/` that CALLS `.canReadObject(`) is honest: the census on origin/main returns exactly the three classified files — `metadata-protocol/src/protocol.ts` (door, search), `service-analytics/src/plugin.ts` (door, aggregate, decision site `api-exposure-door.ts`, which calls `apiExposureDenialReason(` and imports from `@objectstack/spec/data`), `plugin-security/src/security-plugin.ts` (provider). The analytics pin file the table names exists. The three other files that mention the name (`analytics-service.ts`, `read-admission.ts`, the spec contract) mention it in comments or declare it, so the dotted-call matcher has no blind spot among today's mentions. **Right.** Wiring is right too: `@objectstack/core` already declares `packages/**/*.ts` in `cross-package-test-inputs.mjs`, the `repo` vitest project reads `vitest.repo-tests.json`, and the scan copies the sibling `operation-private-keys.pin.test.ts` (same `git grep --untracked`, same `REPO_ROOT`). The header states the doors the discriminator cannot see (share-link, knowledge retrieval) instead of claiming them; see ③.
8. **Behaviour pin** (`protocol.search-api-exposure.test.ts`, 13 cases) holds the card's three pins plus the context-less and `objects=` cases; the negative pins were ablation-verified (old predicate restored: 4 red, 9 green, first failure quoted). **Right.**
9. **Docblock edit in `plugin-approvals` integration test.** The sentence "never consults `apiMethods` at all" became false with this diff; the rewrite keeps the docblock true. Comment-only, test file. **Right.**
10. **Dormancy.** The claim that no shipped object's results change (three `['get']` whitelists all `searchable: false`; nine `[]` whitelists all `apiEnabled: false`; no example app declares `apiMethods`) matches the card's own census and is stated with its limit (deployed and cloud-held definitions not measured). **Right.**

### ② Semver level

- Changeset `.changeset/22640-search-api-exposure.md`: `'@objectstack/metadata-protocol': minor` (a published package, 17.7.0), summary `fix(metadata-protocol)!:`, `**BREAKING**` banner, `Clause-②: no` at line start, one ADR-0087 marker `not-required (no-migration-prescription)` (a category the gate knows). The PR body carries the same `Clause-②: no` at line start. Not `skip-changeset`: the diff publishes. **Matches what the diff publishes.**
- **Level.** The change is an accept-set narrowing, which AGENTS.md classes as BREAKING. Under the launch-window convention (`check-changeset-no-major.mjs`) a breaking change ships as `minor`, with breaking-ness carried by the banner plus the ADR-0087 disposition, not by the level; `patch` is for a `fix(` that changes no public behaviour, which this is not. `minor` is the right level, and the Check Changeset job's ADR-0087 and major-guard steps both concluded success on this head.
- **`Clause-②:` line.** `no` is right. The card narrows a published accept-set and widens no public surface, and the protocol's own rule is that a narrowing card is `Clause-②: no` (it owes this contract-tier review before the queue, which this record is). The `(narrowing)` arm is "at most one arm", one of four breaking-ness carriers; this changeset already carries two others (`!` and the banner) and the gate read `[BREAKING+bang]`. No edit is required; the seat may add the arm as a prose-independent third carrier, but its absence is not a defect.
- ADR-0087 disposition is right on the facts: no spec key, authorable spelling, export or stored shape moves, so `objectstack migrate meta` has nothing to rewrite; the remedy for a surprised author is the declaration they already wrote.

### ③ Boundary flags

Dev flags (from the os-dev-report and the PR body's acceptance notes), each answered:

- **F1 — `Clause-②: no` without the `(narrowing)` arm.** Answered in ②: correct as written; the arm is optional and breaking-ness is carried twice already. No action.
- **F2 — `packages/core/vitest.repo-tests.json` edited, outside the claim's "test files only" surface.** Accepted. It is the list a cross-package test must appear in for `check:cross-package-test-inputs` and turbo hashing to see it; no product code; it was named in the report and the PR body, which is what the claim required of any pin home outside `metadata-protocol`.
- **F3 — the enumeration pin homed in `packages/core`.** Accepted; the claim pre-authorised an outside home when named, and core is the only package whose declared radius already covers `packages/**/*.ts`, so no new declaration was needed.
- **F4 — comment-only edit in `plugin-approvals` integration test docblock.** Accepted (①.9).
- **F5 — zero label writes; labeler-applied labels.** Right per the dispatch; `needs:contract-review` is a marker not a gate, and this record is the PASS it would wait for.
- **F6 — post-sibling (#22646) merge "still owed".** Moot at this read: the PR's merge base d8830c28 IS origin/main. The seat re-reads at queue time as usual.
- **`open_questions`: []** — nothing to answer.

Out-of-scope findings the dev noted and did not file, answered or escalated:

- **Share-link door (`plugin-sharing`) and knowledge retrieval (`service-knowledge`) are named in the pin's header but not held.** Triage's pin asked for every row-serving door "the claimant finds"; these two were found and declared as the discriminator's blind spot rather than silently omitted, and ⛔ no product code outside `searchAll` was the claim's rule, so not touching them is right. **Escalated to the dispatching seat as a decision, non-blocking for this PR:** either file one card for "share-link and knowledge retrieval vs the exposure decision" (share-link serves a record as the system behind an opt-in token; knowledge has no HTTP door in this repository, so the reach question is open) or rule them out by design on the thread. The pin's header is the right place to record whichever answer lands.
- **`service-analytics/src/api-exposure-door.ts` header says the search "reads the same off switch".** Now incomplete, not false; product code outside the claim. A one-line follow-up for the card above or for whoever next touches `service-analytics`. Non-blocking.
- **No `docs/qa/platform-checklist/areas/search.json` item for the exposure skip.** A `checklist-author` sweep item; non-blocking.
- **Docs drift check** lists `content/docs/concepts/metadata-lifecycle.mdx` (via the class symbol) and three release-owned pages. The diff changes no documented API shape, only which objects a sweep serves; nothing in the hand-written page restates the old predicate as a rule as far as this record can read from the inputs. Advisory only.
